title: Overhead Guide Signing: Sign Formats L, M and N (Freeway Lane Assignment)
summary: Sheet 13 of 16 of the overhead guide signing standard. It shows sign formats L, M and N, which are overhead lane assignment panels for freeway access with an Interstate 5 shield, each drawn for two approach lanes. Each format has variants with ONLY boxed arrows or open down arrows and with LEFT LANE and RIGHT LANE wording. Every format refers to the application notes.
description:
Sign L (2 approach lanes shown): three overhead panels, each a rectangle split into a top banner and a bottom row of two cells. The top banner of all three reads Golden State Fwy with an Interstate 5 shield at the right. Panel 1 has two cells, left cell NORTH with a boxed ONLY and a solid down arrow, right cell SOUTH with a boxed ONLY and a solid down arrow. Panel 2 has a left cell with a boxed ONLY and solid down arrow then NORTH, and a right cell SOUTH followed by an open (outline) down arrow. Panel 3 has a left cell with an open down arrow then NORTH, and a right cell with a boxed ONLY and solid down arrow then SOUTH. Each panel is labeled See Notes 11, 13, 14 and 15.

Sign M (2 approach lanes shown): two overhead panels, each with a top banner showing an Interstate 5 shield and the word Freeway, and a bottom row of two cells. Panel 1 has a left cell with an open down arrow then NORTH and a right cell with SOUTH then an open down arrow. Panel 2 has a left cell reading NORTH, LEFT LANE and a right cell reading SOUTH, RIGHT LANE. Each panel is labeled See Notes 11, 13 and 14.

Sign N (2 approach lanes shown): two overhead panels in the same layout as Sign M with the order of the directions reversed. Panel 1 has a left cell with an open down arrow then SOUTH and a right cell with NORTH then an open down arrow. Panel 2 has a left cell reading SOUTH, LEFT LANE and a right cell reading NORTH, RIGHT LANE. Each panel is labeled See Notes 11, 13 and 14.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Overhead Guide Signing, sheet 13 of 16, drawing number S-418.6.
notes:
Sign L (2 approach lanes shown): Golden State Fwy with Interstate 5 shield, NORTH and SOUTH cells with ONLY panels and arrows. See Notes 11, 13, 14 and 15.
Sign M (2 approach lanes shown): Freeway with Interstate 5 shield, NORTH and SOUTH, with arrow and with LEFT LANE and RIGHT LANE variations. See Notes 11, 13 and 14.
Sign N (2 approach lanes shown): Freeway with Interstate 5 shield, SOUTH and NORTH, with arrow and with LEFT LANE and RIGHT LANE variations. See Notes 11, 13 and 14.

title: Overhead Guide Signing: Application Notes 1 through 9
summary: Sheet 15 of 16 of the overhead guide signing standard. It is a text sheet of Application Notes 1 to 9 covering arterial divergences, optional lanes, arrow formats, advance warning plates, destination order, unshadowed turn lanes, the customized R3-2 sign and a five-legged intersection example at Arden and Beverly Boulevards.
description: Text sheet headed Application Notes with nine numbered notes and no drawings. The notes cover divergence signing, elephant track striping per S-491.0, Two-Line Vertical and Diagonal Arrows versus Diagrammatic Arrows, W 61B(CA) warning plates, R3-5 and R3-6 lane assignment signs, arrow position and the order of legends and arrows, unshadowed lanes, the customized R3-2 sign and a five-legged intersection. Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Overhead Guide Signing, sheet 15 of 16, drawing number S-418.6.
notes:
Application Notes
1. At roadway divergences show all arterial street destinations, including those where the street name does not change. This is necessary because sometimes the street name continues on the left leg, sometimes on the right leg and sometimes diverges into two different names.
2. At roadway divergences with two or more approach lanes, utilize elephant track striping as per S-491.0.
3. At roadway divergences use Two-Line Vertical and Diagonal Arrows (with flared tails) over each applicable lane where optional lanes are not involved. However, where optional lanes are involved use Diagrammatic (non-flared) Arrows over each applicable lane in order to better convey the optional lane use.
4. Use the black on yellow "W 61B(CA)" plates to forewarn of the entrapped lane or divergence ahead. However, where the point of divergence is less than 200 feet downstream from the overhead sign, use R3-5 and R3-6 signs to regulate lane assignment.
5. Position arrows as close as practical over the middle of the applicable lanes and position the applicable arterial street destinations preferably above or immediately adjacent to appropriate arrow heads, as space permits. Vertical lines may be shown to distinguish lane groups.
6. Use the single or stacked line destination format in advance of intersections where entrapped turn lanes are not involved. List street and destination names in the following vertical order from the top, associated with the following directional one-line arrows: diagonal-vertical left, horizontal left, diagonal down left, vertical, diagonal-vertical right, horizontal right, and diagonal down right. Show left arrows to the left of the legends and vertical and right arrows to the right of the legends. Show vertical arrows to the left of the legends when the other destinations have right arrows, and to the right when the other destinations have left arrows.
7. At intersections where unshadowed (entrapped) turn lanes or interior optional lanes are involved use R3-5 and R3-6 signs positioned as close as practical over the middle of the applicable lanes.
8. Use the customized R3-2 sign where protected-only phasing is provided for one but not both of the possible left turns, such as the diagonal left-turn but not the sharper left-turn shown.
9. On the diagonal approach of a five-legged intersection the striping can be designed so that the through move is directed to either the right leg or left leg. The combination of striping and overhead signing should be coordinated to clarify and reinforce the intended operation. The first case shows two lanes directed to westbound Arden Boulevard, while the second shows two lanes directed to southbound Beverly Boulevard. Note that some secondary destinations requiring more than a ninety degree turn from an optional lane are not shown, due to space limitations.

title: Overhead Guide Signing: Application Notes 10 through 18
summary: Sheet 16 of 16 of the overhead guide signing standard. It is a text sheet of Application Notes 10 to 18 covering the word To for indirect access, freeway names and shields near interchanges, advance arrow legends, lane assignment sign spacing of 600 to 1300 feet, the W61F(CA) trap lane sign, and bus and carpool panel colors and occupancy legends.
description: Text sheet with nine numbered notes, 10 to 18, and no drawings. The notes cover indirect access to a destination roadway, freeway-to-freeway interchange naming, the Advance Arrow and XXX FT legend, Lane Assignment sign placement 600 to 1300 feet upstream, Down Vertical Arrow format and the LEFT (RIGHT) LANE, NEXT LEFT (RIGHT) and SECOND LEFT (RIGHT) messages, the W61F(CA) sign, bus and carpool panel colors, the S-487.0 reference and occupancy legends. Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Overhead Guide Signing, sheet 16 of 16, drawing number S-418.6.
notes:
10. Where the destination roadway must be accessed via another named roadway the name should be preceded with the word, "To". Ground mounted trailblazer signs should be provided to direct motorist in advance of every decision point enroute to the destination roadway.
11. Where a freeway on-ramp is within one mile of a freeway-to-freeway interchange, the full freeway name should be shown followed by the appropriate route shield and number. However, in constrained situations the full freeway name may be deleted. In all other situations the appropriate route shield and number followed by the word, "Fwy" or "Freeway" is sufficient.
12. Use the Advance Arrow and "XXX FT" legends where there is an intervening roadway 100 feet or less upstream of the overhead sign.
13. Lane Assignment signs should be provided 600 to 1300 feet upstream of turns or divergences associated with grade separations.
14. For Lane Assignment signs use the Down Vertical Arrow format where there is an entrapped turn lane or where it is possible to position arrows over each of the applicable lanes. They should be placed as close as practical over the middle of each lane. Where this is not possible use the "LEFT (RIGHT) LANE" or "NEXT LEFT (RIGHT)" format. The "NEXT LEFT (RIGHT)" message may be used only where there is no intervening intersection. The "SECOND LEFT (RIGHT)" message may be used instead of "NEXT LEFT (RIGHT)" where there is close spacing between intersections.
15. The black-on-yellow "W61F(CA)" sign is used for advance warning of a trap lane, per S-491.0.
16. The sign panel pertaining to the bus and carpool lane shall have a black legend on a white background and the diamond shall be white legend on a black background.
17. See S-487.0 for exclusive bus lane striping.
18. For exclusive lanes where two-person carpools are allowed it is not necessary to identify the required vehicle occupancy. Other required occupancies shall be identified with and below the diamond symbol.

title: On-Street Angle Parking Stalls (Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of the City of Los Angeles standard for on-street angle parking stalls, approved 9/18/2020. It shows parking meter locations, a plan of 9 ft by 16 ft angled stalls with a 2 ft maximum overhang and a table of dimensions A, B, C and E for angles from 37.5 to 75 degrees. Notes set thermoplastic material, design basis and the minimum E dimension by street type.
description:
Parking meter locations view: a plan strip with a travel lane between two bands of diagonal hatching, one band along each curb face. The upper curb face carries meters at P=4' spacing and the hatched band is 20" deep, measured from the curb face. The lower curb face carries meters at P=2' spacing, also with a 20" dimension. Between the bands, a 4" Y EDGE LINE (yellow) and a 4" W EDGE LINE (white) are called out, and two open arrows point right in the lane. A dimension W is marked across one of the hatched bands.

Stall plan: a plan of angled stalls against a curb face, with a vehicle in two stalls. A 2' MAX. OVERHANG callout shows the vehicle front extending past the curb face. Stalls are 9'X16' with 4" W stall lines drawn as double lines with 10" dimensions at the stall end. Angle phi is measured between the curb face and the stall line. Dimension B is the stall width measured along the curb, C is the spacing along the curb between stall lines at the next stall, A is the perpendicular depth from curb face, and 7' CLEAR is the clear width between stalls. 16' is the stall length and 9' the stall width. E is the distance from the stall ends to the 4" W EDGE LINE (SEE NOTES 3 &4). Below it, the travel lane is 10' MIN. wide with an open arrow pointing left, bounded by the 4" W EDGE LINE at the stall side and a lane line, double yellow, 4" dashed yellow line, or 4" yellow edge line at the opposite side.

Table of angle dimensions (theta, A, B, C, E): 37.5 deg: A 16.9', B 14.8', C 22', E 11'. 45 deg: A 17.7', B 12.7', C 17.7', E 11.1'. 50 deg: A 18.0', B 11.75', C 15.1', E 12'. 52.5 deg: A 18.2', B 11.3', C 13.9', E 13.1'. 60 deg: A 18.4', B 10.4', C 10.6', E 15.1'. 67.5 deg: A 18.2', B 9.7', C 7.5', E 17.3'. 75 deg: A 17.8', B 9.3', C 4.8', E 19.7'.

Title block: approved 9/18/2020, signed for Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, On-Street Angle Parking Stalls, sheet 1 of 2, drawing number S-440.0.
notes:
Notes
1. All parking stall lines and edge lines shall be in alkyd-based thermoplastic.
2. Calculations based on, but not limited to Los Angeles Municipal Code (L.A.M.C.), Section 12.21, utilizing 9'x16' stall size. Large vehicles requiring the 18-foot dimension are expected to overhang the curb, as shown. Stall design above requires 2-foot overhang for 18-foot vehicle.
3. On local streets, collector streets, and those arterial streets which function as collector streets (see 4, below), the "E" dimension shall be 4' minimum where the parking angle is greater than 45 degrees. On those local and collector streets with angle parking 45 degrees or less, the "E" dimension may be reduced to a minimum of 2 feet. The 4' dimension is preferred, however, and should be provided if the roadway width permits.
4. On arterial highways, the "E" dimensions shown in the above table shall be considered required minimums. This is intended to provide for maneuvers to and from the parking stall without obstructing traffic movement in the adjacent traveled lane. Arterial streets are designated in community plans. A designated arterial street may, for the purposes of this standard plan be considered as a collector street if the daily volume is less than 10,000 vehicles, or the striping provides for only one through lane in each direction.

Notes

title: Narrowed Roadway Delineation (Without Lane Drop)
summary: Standard drawing S-444.0, approved September 20, 2005, for striping a roadway that narrows without dropping a lane. Case 1 and Case 2 show an 8 inch white channelizing line with 12 inch white diagonals, and Table 1 gives preferred taper rates from 15:1 at 25 mph to 60:1 at 55 mph. Six notes give when to install the line and how to set taper rates.
description:
Case 1 (plan): a travel lane heading up the sheet with a dashed lane line on the left. On the right, the roadway edge line runs straight and the roadway narrows by an 8" white channelizing line that tapers diagonally toward the right edge. The line starts from a straight offset line at the top, where the legend reads 2' OFF RECOMMENDED, with (1' MINIMUM, 7' MINIMUM W/PARKING). A SW44(CA) (DOWN LEFT ARROW) sign is placed at the start of the taper. Inside the taper triangle are 12" WHITE DIAGONALS, SPACING PER PLAN (MINIMUM TWO DIAGONALS). Labels: LANE LINE, and 8" WHITE LINE (SEE NOTES 1 & 2). At the bottom, 2' OR EDGE OF GUTTER IF PARKING IS PROHIBITED, 8' IF PARKING IS PERMITTED, is the offset from the edge line to the channelizing line. A hollow arrow shows travel direction up the sheet.

Case 2 (plan): the same taper and diagonals, labeled LANE LINE (SEE NOTE 3) and 8" WHITE LINE (SEE NOTE 3). Here the lane width at the start of the taper is dimensioned 10' TO 12' from the lane line to the edge line, with the same 2' OR EDGE OF GUTTER IF PARKING IS PROHIBITED, 8' IF PARKING IS PERMITTED offset and the same 2' OFF RECOMMENDED, 1' MINIMUM, 7' MINIMUM W/PARKING legend at the top. The SW44(CA) sign is shown as a diamond sign with a down-left arrow.

Table 1 (speed limit in mph, preferred taper rate): 25 mph, 15:1. 30 mph, 20.5:1. 35 mph, 26.7:1. 40 mph, 45:1. 45 mph, 50:1. 50 mph, 55:1. 55 mph, 60:1.

Title block: approved September 20, 2005, signed for Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Narrowed Roadway Delineation (Without Lane Drop), sheet 1 of 1, drawing number S-444.0.
notes:
Notes:
1. For Case 1 the 8" channelizing line should be installed where: A) downstream lane width is less than 13' (lane line to edge line) with parking prohibited; or B) downstream lane width is less than 20' (lane line to edge of roadway) with parking permitted; or C) the change in roadway width is 6' or greater.
2. For Case 1 the 8" white edgeline should be a minimum of 100 feet in length where conditions permit, to provide adequate visibility for approaching motorists. Taper rates in Case 1 should be 5:1 or greater.
3. For Case 2 the lane line and 8" channelizing line may be transitioned using the appropriate minimum taper rate from Table 1 or by appropriate curve-tangent-curve design.
4. For narrowed roadway delineation with a lane drop see S-485.0.
5. For Case 1 and Case 2, the addition of 12" white diagonals should be installed to emphasize that large pavement areas are not intended as part of the travelled roadway.
6. Taper rates shown in Table 1 are based on posted speed plus 5 mph. Where the 85% speed (critical speed) on the approach is determined to be equal to the posted speed, the table numbers for the next lower speed increment may be used.

title: Typical Placement of Pavement Turn Arrows
summary: Standard drawing S-456.0, approved March 13, 2006, showing typical placement of pavement turn arrows at an intersection approach. Left and right turn arrows are placed at the beginning of each turn lane, with a second arrow at L/2 only if the turn lane length L1 or L2 is 250 feet or more.
description:
Plan view: a typical four-leg intersection with curb returns at all four corners, a central rectangle for the intersection, and lane lines on each approach. The sheet focuses on the lower approach, which has a left-turn lane on the left side and right-turn lane on the right side, separated from through lanes by dashed lane lines, with a solid line at the left edge of the lanes. A double yellow centerline curves into the left-turn pocket. In the left turn pocket, two left-turn arrows are drawn: one at the beginning of the lane at the bottom of the length L1, and one at the middle at L1/2 measured from the stop line. In the right turn lane, two right-turn arrows are drawn: one at the beginning of the lane at length L2 and one at L2/2. Dimension L1 is the full length of the left-turn lane and L1/2 is half of it. Dimension L2 is the full length of the right-turn lane and L2/2 is half of it. Callout in pink highlight with leader lines to both arrows at the half-length position: Install only if L1 or L2 >= 250'. A second pink callout with leader lines to the arrows at the lane start: Install at beginning of lane.

Title block: approved March 13, 2006, signed for Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Typical Placement of Pavement Turn Arrows, sheet 1 of 1, drawing number S-456.0.
notes: Install only if L1 or L2 is 250 feet or greater (greater than or equal to 250'). Install at beginning of lane.

title: Crosswalk Alignment (Sheet 2 of 2): Notes
summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of standard S-490.0 is a notes-only sheet for crosswalk alignment at curb returns. It sets the A, B and C offsets for crosswalks served by an access ramp (A and B at least 2 ft, C at most 7 ft, preferred C of 4 ft), adjusts C for small curb radii, requires realignment of all crosswalks when one is modified, calls for unidirection ramps where one ramp does not fit, and sets crosswalk width at 15 ft standard or 20 ft in high pedestrian areas.
description: Text sheet headed NOTES with six numbered notes and no drawings. The notes refer to dimensions A, B and C and to Case 1 and Case 2 situations that are drawn on sheet 1 of 2. Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Crosswalk Alignment, drawing number S-490.0, sheet 2 of 2.
notes:
Notes
1. Crosswalk installations with an access ramp intended to serve Case 1 situations generally should be aligned so that A >= 2', B >= 2' and C <= 7'. However, if there is an all-day parking lane, a parallel approach right-turn lane or if the curb lane width for parallel through traffic is >= 14', the related A or B distance may be >= 0.
2. Countless combinations of existing intersectional angles, curb radii and ramp locations prevent selection of specific dimensions for A, B, and C in Case 1 situations. C should be set at a preferred 4' dimension wherever the criteria for A and B are met. However, at a right angle intersection with an existing ramp located at the M.C. and curb return radius of <17', C must be <4' in order for A and B to be the desired 2' minimum needed when through curb lanes are <= 14'. For a curb radius of 14', set C=3' so that A & B are equal to 2. C dimensions for curb radii between 14' and 17' may be increased proportionately to 4'. For curb radii <13', set the C distance at the edge of gutter (generally 1' to 2') when curb lanes are <= 14'. With these smaller radii where curb lanes are >14', the A and B distances should be decreased to 0 to achieve a larger C dimension.
3. At intersections where street resurfacing, street widening, or channelization projects require reinstallation or modification of an existing crosswalk, all crosswalks at the intersection should be realigned to meet the criteria of Notes 1 and 2 above.
4. At curb returns without a ramp where a single ramp location would not meet the criteria of Note 1 above, unidirection ramps should be proposed, as shown in Case 2.
5. For Case 2 situations, C <= 2'.
6. A crosswalk width of 15' is standard. Use 20' in high pedestrian areas, or on the receptive leg of dual left turns.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing (Sheet 1 of 7)
summary: Sheet 1 of 7 of standard S-497.0, approved 12/26/2000. It supplements Table 1 of Section 521 and gives Table A of minimum sight distances for permissive left turns, from 165 ft at 15 mi/hr to 620 ft at 55 mi/hr, based on a gap time of 5.0 plus 0.5 n seconds. Five notes explain permanent restrictions and sight distance blocked by opposing left-turn queues.
description:
Table A: Minimum Sight Distance Requirements for Permissive Left Turns, * ft (rounded). Rows are speed limit or advisory speed in mi/hr and columns are gap times by number of opposing through lanes: 5.5 sec for 1 lane, 6.0 sec for 2 lane, 6.5 sec for 3 lane and 7.0 sec for 4 lane. Rows: 15 mi/hr: 165, 180, 195, 210. 20 mi/hr: 205, 220, 240, 260. 25 mi/hr: 240, 260, 290, 310. 30 mi/hr: 280, 310, 330, 360. 35 mi/hr: 320, 350, 380, 410. 40 mi/hr: 360, 400, 430, 460. 45 mi/hr: 400, 440, 480, 510. 50 mi/hr: 440, 480, 520, 570. 55 mi/hr: 480, 530, 570, 620. Footnote: *Based on the speed limit or advisory speed plus 5 mi/hr.

The rest of the sheet is notes text. Title block: approved 12/26/2000, signed Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing, sheet 1 of 7, drawing number S-497.0.
notes:
Notes:
1. This standard plan supplements Table 1 of Section 521, pertaining to restricted sight distance which justifies protected left-turn phasing at signalized intersections.
2. Motorists require both an acceptable gap in opposing traffic and sufficient sight distance in order to execute permissive left turns. Studies have shown that the value of an acceptable gap is equal to (5.0 + 0.5 n) seconds of travel time, where "n" is the number of opposing through lanes. Sufficient sight distance is the distance associated with an acceptable gap, or the gap time multiplied by the design speed. The design speed for opposing through traffic is five miles per hour above the posted or prima facie speed limit. However, where there is restrictive horizontal or vertical alignment the design speed is five miles per hour above the posted advisory speed. See Table 1.
3. Several types of sight distance restrictions can occur. Permanent type restrictions, due to horizontal curvature, vertical alignment or physical obstructions cannot be readily overcome. Where the sight distances for permanent type restrictions are less than that shown in Table A, and left turns are allowed then protected left-turn phasing is required. See Figures 1, 2 and 3 which illustrate these types of restrictions.
4. Sight distance also can be restricted due to opposing left turn vehicles at locations where left turn lanes are negatively offset. Where the opposing left turn demand is light it tends to be accommodated during the same signal cycle of arrival. In this case, left turn motorists would be afforded adequate sight distance to execute left turns at some point during the green or yellow after opposing left turn motorists clear. Thus, protected left turn phasing would not be necessary. See Figure 4. However, where an opposing left turn queue is frequent and persistent and the sight distances are less than those shown in Table A then left turn motorists are not afforded an opportunity to turn with adequate sight distance. In this case, island removal with restriping or protected left-turn phasing is necessary and required. See Figure 5.
5. A unique situation occurs with negatively offset left turn lanes in combination with a right horizontal curve. As illustrated in Figure 6, left turn motorists can see opposing through traffic both upstream from the front and downstream from the back of a left turn queue. However, motorists cannot continuously see downstream from the front of the queue. If the required sight distance is at a point which is not obstructed by the opposing queue then protected left turn phasing would not be necessary. However, where the required sight distance is at a point which is obstructed by the opposing queue then visibility is inadequate for left turning decisions and protected left turn phasing is required.
